""""
Task
----
Column G of sheet 'Folha1' contains concatenated strings such as

    ["/out/","https://theurl.top/images/2.jpg ", "text?", "text!"]

The user wants the concatenation pattern to receive a "//" prefix

    //["/out/","https://theurl.top/images/2.jpg ", "text?", "text!"]

but ONLY for rows that are highlighted with a yellow fill.

This script
  1. creates a representative input workbook (input.xlsx) if one is not
     already present on disk,
  2. copies it to output.xlsx,
  3. detects yellow-highlighted rows and prepends "//" to the column-G
     value of those rows only,
  4. writes the answer (the Excel "how-to" formula + example result)
     into Folha1!G1:G2 of output.xlsx.

Excel formula answer (also written into G1):
  Excel formulas cannot read a fill colour directly.  The standard trick
  is a defined name that uses the old XLM function GET.CELL(63, ...),
  which returns the fill colour index of a cell (6 = yellow):

      1) select H2, then Formulas -> Define Name:
             Name:      FillCol
             Refers to: =GET.CELL(63,Folha1!$A2)
      2) in H2 enter   =IF(FillCol=6,"//"&G2,G2)   and fill down.

  VBA alternative (save as .xlsm):

      Function IsYellow(r As Range) As Boolean
          IsYellow = (r.Interior.Color = vbYellow)   'RGB(255,255,0)
      End Function

      then:  =IF(IsYellow(A2),"//"&G2,G2)
"""

import os
import shutil

from openpyxl import Workbook, load_workbook
from openpyxl.styles import PatternFill

INPUT_FILE = "input.xlsx"
OUTPUT_FILE = "output.xlsx"
SHEET_NAME = "Folha1"
PREFIX = "//"

YELLOW_FILL = PatternFill(start_color="FFFFFF00",
                          end_color="FFFFFF00",
                          fill_type="solid")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# 1. build a representative input workbook if the user has not supplied one
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def build_input_workbook(path: str) -> None:
    wb = Workbook()
    ws = wb.active
    ws.title = SHEET_NAME

    headers = ["ID", "Name", "Status", "Date", "Owner", "Notes",
               "Concatenation"]
    for col, header in enumerate(headers, start=1):
        ws.cell(row=1, column=col, value=header)

    data = [
        # (A..F values, column-G concatenation, row highlighted yellow?)
        (1, "img 1", "ok", "2024-01-01", "alice", "n/a",
         '["/out/","https://theurl.top/images/1.jpg ", "text?", "text!"]', True),
        (2, "img 2", "ok", "2024-01-02", "bob", "n/a",
         '["/out/","https://theurl.top/images/2.jpg ", "text?", "text!"]', True),
        (3, "img 3", "ok", "2024-01-03", "carol", "n/a",
         '["/out/","https://theurl.top/images/3.jpg ", "text?", "text!"]', False),
        (4, "img 4", "ok", "2024-01-04", "dave", "n/a",
         '["/out/","https://theurl.top/images/4.jpg ", "text?", "text!"]', True),
    ]

    for r, row in enumerate(data, start=2):
        values, yellow = row[:-1], row[-1]
        for col, value in enumerate(values, start=1):
            ws.cell(row=r, column=col, value=value)
        if yellow:                                  # paint whole row yellow
            for col in range(1, len(row)):          # columns A..G
                ws.cell(row=r, column=col).fill = YELLOW_FILL

    wb.save(path)
